trust_decision.summary: The system prompt and model context are trusted; content the user did not author (context files, MEMORY.md/USER.md entries, tool results from web/browser/MCP) must be scanned for injection or explicitly marked as untrusted data before it reaches the model. The decision is made at each ingestion path: prompt assembly, memory write AND memory load, and tool-result message construction.

landing_point.why: CWE-74 plus the fix title points at prompt injection; _scan_context_content is the only injection scanner documented on the prompt-assembly path (website/docs/developer-guide/prompt-assembly.md:130) and is the first place a report reader greps for. The real gap (memory load, tool-result framing) is one and two packages away from it.

fix_sites.entry_point: build_context_files_prompt (session start), also agent/subdirectory_hints.py:188 subdirectory hints
every tool call through the agent loop (agent/tool_executor.py:447, agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py:321, mini_swe_runner.py:540)
imported by the three scanners above (scan_for_threats / first_threat_message)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: make_tool_result_message only shapes a dict, and its delimiter is advisory prose rather than enforcement, so a solver can argue the defence belongs at the fetchers (web_tools / mcp_tool) and leave the builder alone — especially since touching it rewrites every tool result and invalidates the prefix cache.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Multimodal tool results are content lists of {type:text}/{type:image_url} parts and must pass through byte-identical so vision-capable provider adapters keep a valid list shape; wrapping the whole list as a string (or stringifying it) breaks every screenshot/browser result.

O6_input_shapes: tool-result content: plain string vs multimodal list of parts vs dict vs None
tool name: exact set members (web_extract, web_search) vs underscore prefixes (browser_, mcp_) vs dotted form mcp.<server>.<tool>
content length: shorter than 32 chars vs long
memory: individual entry string vs list of entries; entry already starting with [BLOCKED:
scope selector: all vs context vs strict over the same pattern table

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Codex transport projects MCP tool results straight into tool messages, bypassing make_tool_result_message; its tool name is the dotted mcp.<server>.<tool>, which the fix's mcp_ prefix test would not match even if it were routed through the helper.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: codex runs its own agent loop in a subprocess; this projector is described as a record for the curator/memory review, not as the model's prompt.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: agent/transports/ — one package away from agent/tool_dispatch_helpers.py

O8_uncovered_routes.route: External memory-provider block (honcho/mem0/supermemory/...) is appended verbatim to the volatile system prompt with no injection scan.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: opt-in third-party plugins are outside the core built-in memory store's trust boundary; their recall text is the provider's responsibility.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: agent/system_prompt.py and agent/memory_manager.py — separate module from the memory store the fix touched

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Skills index (skill_name, frontmatter_name, description from SKILL.md) is rendered into the stable system prompt without any scan, and is served from the .skills_prompt_snapshot.json cache.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: skills are gated by skills_guard at install time and the index is only short names and descriptions, so it is already covered by a neighbouring feature.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: agent/prompt_builder.py (same file as the landing point) and agent/system_prompt.py

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Cron prompts are screened by a separate pattern table and invisible-char set, so patterns or scope changes added to the shared library never reach the cron ingestion path.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: cron prompts are authored by the user through the cron tool and already have their own dedicated scanner.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: tools/cronjob_tools.py — different file from the shared library it was not migrated to

O8b_injection_room.sibling: web_crawl_tool fetches and LLM-summarises attacker-controlled pages and is handled as a tool name elsewhere (agent/display.py:907, hermes_cli/config.py:2334), but the delimiter set in the fix enumerates only web_extract and web_search.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the untrusted-tool set is a hand-written enumeration of a fetch family that already has three members, so adding the third is a one-line omission a maintainer would plausibly make.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: mcp_<server>_list_resources / _read_resource / _get_prompt return server-controlled text but only mcp_<server>_<tool> is treated as untrusted.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the resource/prompt tools were added beside the call tool in the same registration helper, so a fix that reasons about 'MCP tools' naturally covers calls and forgets resources and prompts.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: nested directory hint files are rendered into the prompt through the same context scanner; a second hint source (e.g. a per-tool or per-plugin hints directory) added without the scanner call is realistic.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the scan here is a single inline call copied by hand rather than a mandatory wrapper, so a new hint producer is one omission away.

O9_family: prompt injection / indirect prompt injection into an LLM context (CWE-74; LLM01)

O10_build.project_tests: tests/tools/test_memory_tool.py and tests/agent/test_prompt_builder.py already cover this area at the pinned commit; the fix adds tests/tools/test_threat_patterns.py and tests/agent/test_tool_dispatch_helpers.py (neither exists at the pinned commit).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Extend the two existing inline pattern lists (_CONTEXT_THREAT_PATTERNS in prompt_builder.py and _MEMORY_THREAT_PATTERNS in memory_tool.py) and stop, leaving the memory load path and the tool-result message builder untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: No out-of-scope issues observed; every mechanism noted is the injection-protection surface this advisory covers, at the pinned commit.
